title: the plugin steers the running turn
intent: The orchestrator can send a message to a running agent without replacing the turn: that is steering, and a provider declares it with the capability `prompt.steer'.  The ACP adapter of the orchestrator's library does not know the capability -- it announces four capabilities and has no `prompt.steer' -- and a request with `delivery: "steer"' does not reach the kernel at all: the adapter interrupts the running turn and starts a new one.  That is a replacement, not steering, and the orchestrator refuses the request outright when the provider does not declare the capability ('Provider does not support prompt.steer').  What changes: the plugin declares the capability -- in the connection and in the session it opens -- and translates such a request into `session/steer' of the kernel, which the kernel already knows (`lib/yeah-acp.el').  The request never reaches the adapter, so the running turn is not interrupted, and the orchestrator is answered with the identifier of the turn that is running, which is what it checks.  Two facts are needed for the translation and both come from the wire: the identifier of the session of the kernel (the orchestrator knows only its own) and the identifier of the running turn.  The first is learned from the answer of the kernel to `session/new', and the session of the orchestrator is named by a mark the plugin puts into the parameters of the open -- the adapter carries it into `_meta' without change.  The second is learned from the events of the adapter: the turn that starts is the turn that runs.  The check runs the plugin's own code against the real kernel: the plugin raises the core through `ensureService', talks to it through `yeahTransport', `yeahSteerWire' and `yeahSteerConnection', and the kernel -- real, with a fake model whose turn never ends -- receives the steering as `session/steer' naming its own session and the text of the message, while it never receives `session/cancel' and the adapter never sees the request.  The capability is declared only when the orchestrator offers it: a connection that chose an unoffered capability is not accepted at all, so an older host keeps its own refusal.
checks: cd plugin/yeah-provider && npm run typecheck && npm test
objection: The wave does not change the adapter of the orchestrator's library: the plugin declares the capability and translates the request itself, and the adapter of the library still replaces a turn when it is given a steering request.  The wave does not prove the steering through the real orchestrator: the check drives the plugin's code and a fake adapter, and the live proof is deferred to the live run of the package.  The wave does not prove that the clarification reaches the model in the middle of the turn: the kernel answers `session/steer' with the identifier of the queued input, and the model takes it after the current batch of tools -- that is the kernel's own rule for steering, and it is not what this wave is about.  The wave does not make the steering timely over stdio: over a pipe the kernel reads the next request only after the turn has settled, so the steering is read late and becomes an ordinary ask; the service placement of wave 72 is what makes a request during a turn read while the turn runs, and the check of this wave runs in that placement.  The wave does not make steering work for an agent that is not Yeah: `session/steer' is the kernel's own method, an extension of ACP, and a provider of another kind answers it in its own way.  The wave leaves the decision of the owner untouched: whether the orchestrator offers `prompt.steer' to a plugin is the orchestrator's business, and the plugin only answers what it was offered.
refuted_by: the plugin does not declare the steering capability, or the request with `delivery: "steer"' does not reach the core as `session/steer', or the running turn is interrupted, or the steering request reaches the adapter that replaces the turn, or the orchestrator is answered with another turn, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The control of the claim was applied to a copy of the tree and bit by the assertion of the check and not by a crash: the plugin stopped recognising the steering request (`prompt.delivery === "never"'), and the check ended with the code 1 and with its own words -- 'the kernel did not receive the steering', 'the steering request reached the adapter that replaces the turn' and 'the plugin did not report the identifier of the running turn'.  The clean tree ended with the code 0, and it ended with the code 0 in a copy without `node_modules' as well: the module of the steering carries no dependency of the library of the orchestrator, so the check needs neither the dependencies of the plugin nor the network.  The tests of the plugin pass (67 of them, 7 of them new).  The way the plugin learns the session of the kernel depends on the adapter of the library: it copies the parameters of the provider into `_meta' of the request `session/new' without change, and the mark of the plugin rides there.  When that copy disappears, the steering refuses itself with the words 'the core does not know this session' -- the failure is honest and it does not steer the wrong session.
